correctness.rationale: For every r>0, C>0, lambda>=0, q in (0,1], renewal intervisit time T>0 with finite mean m, the stationary visit-epoch expectation contracts. Exact renewal rate H=q r C/((r+lambda)m)*(1-phi)/(1-(1-q)phi) holds with phi=E exp(-(r+lambda)T). Jensen proves deterministic fixed-mean optimality. Explicit Poisson-vs-periodic comparison is R_q(x)=(x+q)(exp(x)-1)/(x*(exp(x)-1+q))>1; derivative in q positive, so maximize at q=1; derivative in x changes sign exactly once at unique root exp(x)=1+x+x^2. Maximum R*=1.298425607525639, equality only q=1,x=x*. Checker replay passed 90810 diagnostics and independent Monte Carlo comparisons. The proof, not the numerical checks, establishes quantifiers and uniqueness.

originality.rationale: The claimed new component is the sharp parameter-uniform 29.842560752564 percent *relative* limit, its equality conditions and its validity with fractional focal harvesting plus Poisson competitor clearing. Possingham (1989) already proved the qualitative advantage of regular sampling under decelerating resource renewal; that qualitative fact is excluded. Ohashi and Thomson (2005) simulate different replenishment laws and complete harvest; Korman et al. (2020) optimize purely stochastic strategies with linear discrete replenishment. The inspected material gives no mathematical implication of the specific sharp universal ratio, although earlier full texts and unexamined renewal theory remain priority risks.

value.rationale: A natural model of resource regeneration, competitor clearing and incompletely emptying focal visits motivates quantifying the maximum relative effect of temporal regularity at fixed mean frequency. The dimensionless 29.84256 percent bound is sharp over all positive recovery rates, competitor hazards, harvest fractions and mean intervals, with equality conditions. It offers a reusable quantitative ecological benchmark beyond a simple Jensen sign deduction. The model deliberately does not claim energetic optimization, route design, empirical predictiveness or a theorem for other renewal laws.
